text: The 'same as the timestamp-free form' tests can pass vacuously: the timestamped diff -u and diff -ru both give zero roots today, so equality alone proves nothing. Assert the exact result: exit 0, exactly PostSalesDoc, entries non-empty, no changed-root diagnostics; for the deletion, the exact diagnostic kind and file and exit 2 (sol #1, opus #5)
evidence: Design rewritten: C1/C3 assert exit 0, roots exactly PostSalesDoc, entries non-empty, no changedRootsDiagnostics, plus equality; C2 asserts exit 2 and exactly one {kind: diff-file-deleted, file: ./src/subscriber.al}, no diff-file-unmatched; every test 'asserts an EXACT expected result, never only equal to the other form'.

text: One mutation (drop the TAB cut) cannot discriminate every test: the git escaped-\t and space+TAB forms pass with or without the cut. Give each test its own break and record its failure (sol #2, opus #4)
evidence: Design names a break per test: C1-C3 drop the TAB cut; C4 cut after unquote_path instead of before; U2 cut at the first space instead of TAB (space case) and drop the C-unescape of \t (tab case); U1 asserts path, kind and hunks.

text: P7 (a raw TAB never belongs to a path) was asserted, not shown, and its claim that GNU diff does not quote is false: diffutils 3.12 C-quotes names with a space, TAB or quote and puts the TAB after the closing quote (sol #3, opus #1)
evidence: Conductor captured the real bytes: P7b (git 2.53.0, with and without core.quotePath=false: `--- "a/with\ttab.al"$`, `--- a/with space.al^I$`) and P7c (GNU diffutils 3.12: `--- "o/sp ace.al"^I<time>$`, `--- "o/t\tab.al"^I<time>$`). P7 rewritten as a wire-format statement with the residual stated (only a producer writing a TAB-containing name raw and unquoted); the exact bytes become test literals.

text: The test list misses GNU's quoted form with a timestamp, `"./src/a b.al"<TAB><time>`, the one shape where cutting at the TAB BEFORE unquoting matters (opus #2)
evidence: Design adds C4 (a fixture file with a space in its name, header `--- "./src/a b.al"<TAB><time>`, matched, exit 0; break: cut after unquote_path → unmatched); the Design states unquote_path now receives the quoted form without the trailing TAB/time it cannot unquote today.

text: diff -ruN never writes /dev/null for a deleted file (real path with the epoch time, `@@ -1 +0,0 @@`) and plain diff -ru reports a deletion only as `Only in`, so a directory diff never yields DiffFileDeleted; list it as a non-goal and file it as a discovery (opus #3)
evidence: Verified by the conductor on GNU diffutils 3.12 (P7c). Design non-goals now list `Only in` deletions and diff -ruN's epoch-dated real-path deletion (after this change it reads as a modified file with every line deleted), filed as a discovery. Not needed for the acceptance, which names a /dev/null deletion.

text: Boundary coverage: no timestamped `--- /dev/null` addition case, no CRLF or spaces-before-TAB case, and the CLI roots do not tell Added from Modified; add parser assertions for path, kind, hunks (sol #4, opus #6)
evidence: Design adds U1: `--- /dev/null<TAB><time>` with a real `+++` path is an ADDED file; CRLF line endings and spaces before the TAB give the same path; path, kind and hunks asserted.

text: Scope wording conflict: 'a raw TAB never belongs to a path' versus excluding file names that contain a TAB; distinguish raw TAB bytes in headers from decoded TABs in quoted names (sol #5)
evidence: P7 and the Design now separate the header wire format (a raw TAB byte only ends the path) from a name's own TAB (quoted as the escaped two characters \t, decoded after the cut); file names containing a TAB are SUPPORTED via quoting; only an unquoted raw-TAB name from an old producer is the residual.

text: The #76 T3 doc comment says plain diff -u's tab and timestamp are not stripped; it becomes stale (sol #6)
evidence: Conductor verified :2354-2356 (P8); the Design lists updating that comment as part of the change.

text: `split('\t').next().unwrap_or(rest)` has an unreachable unwrap_or; use split_once (opus #7)
evidence: Design now reads `let rest = rest.split_once('\t').map_or(rest, |(path, _)| path);`.

text: Pre-existing: unquote_path trims the path, so a git name with a trailing space loses it; not caused by this change (opus #8)
evidence: Pre-existing and independent of the TAB rule; listed in the Design's non-goals and filed as a discovery so it is tracked, not lost.

text: U2's tab-case break 'drop the C-unescape of \t' changes unquote_path, not the new cut, so it only shows the test reads the decoded name, not U2's claim that the TAB rule leaves git's escaped \t alone; use 'cut after unquote_path' (C4's break), which turns the decoded name into a/with (opus r2 N1)
evidence: Design U2 now uses, for the tab case, 'cut AFTER unquote_path (the same break as C4: the decoded TAB is then cut and the name becomes a/with)'; the unescape break may run as a second break and is labelled as only showing the test reads the decoded name. Design-section hash f2d7215c6520765b.

text: Now that diff -ru headers match, `Only in <dir>: <file>` lines (added or deleted files) fall into 'All other lines ignored' with no diagnostic, so a diff that adds or removes files succeeds and silently leaves their roots out; before #111 the same diff failed loudly (every header unmatched, exit 2). Report them (code-review #1)
evidence: Conductor verified: diff_parser.rs:759 `// All other lines ignored` is the fall-through for `Only in` lines. Fixed in 042764fe: DiffParseResult gains a documented `only_in: Vec<String>`; parse_unified_diff reads `Only in <dir>: <name>` (split at the first `: `) and records `<dir>/<name>` as written; digest_cli pushes one DiffFileUnmatched { file } per entry, like any other unmapped file in a partly mapped diff. New unit test only_in_lines_are_recorded. Proofs: B5 (restore the ignore) fails the unit test (left [] vs both paths) and C3; B6 (digest_cli drops only_in) fails C3. Adding/deleting from `Only in` stays a non-goal (discovery).

text: C3 locks in the silent drop: its diff carries `Only in ../old/src: subscriber.al` and the test requires exit 0 and no diagnostic (code-review #2)
evidence: C3 now asserts exactly one diagnostic {kind: diff-file-unmatched, file: ../old/src/subscriber.al}, entries non-empty, roots exactly PostSalesDoc, exit 0; its equality with the diff -u form is dropped and its doc comment updated. Red before the fix (`left: []` at :2460, a1-r1-red-cli.log); fails under B5, B6 and re-run B1.

text: The TAB cut discards the timestamp, which under `diff -N` (epoch, in local time) is the only sign of a missing file: -ruN deletions read as Modified -> diff-file-unmatched, -N additions as Modified with an invented old_path (code-review #3)
evidence: A stated non-goal of the converged design (S1-5): -ruN epoch-dated deletions are listed under 'Not covered' in the CHANGELOG and filed as a discovery (ledger Discoveries). They fail loudly as diff-file-unmatched, not silently; a -N addition reads as Modified with every line added, which still roots the file's routines. Recognising the epoch (in any timezone) is the discovery's work.

text: 'reads plain diff -u / diff -ru headers' over-claims: `diff -ru old new` run from the parent folder writes `n/src/m.al`; neither strip_ab_prefix nor normalize_input removes the tree-root folder, so such files stay diff-file-unmatched; C3 passes only because its headers use ./src/ (code-review #4)
evidence: 042764fe's CHANGELOG: plain headers are read when their paths are relative to the workspace (run diff from the workspace root, or use --label); `diff -ru old new` run from a parent folder still writes a tree-root folder (`n/src/…`) that is not matched.

text: The `Only in` arm reads any top-level line, so an `Only in X: Y` line in a git format-patch commit message adds a false diff-file-unmatched; loud, not silent; roots unaffected (opus r2 N2)

Tightening it (accept `Only in` only before any `diff --git` section) is a small follow-up; not worth a code change and a further gate in the last rounds for a diagnostic-only false positive in commit-message text.
